patch_description: Fundamentally different approach: instead of blind stochastic hill-climbing on a soft surrogate, use directed subgradient ascent on the hard objective. At each iteration we identify all near-minimal triangles, compute the exact analytic gradient of their (signed) area with respect to each vertex, and move only the vertices involved in the bottleneck triangles in the direction that increases the minimum. This is combined with (1) a short simulated-annealing exploration phase using coordinated group moves, (2) many structured boundary-heavy seeds (known to be good for Heilbronn n=11), and (3) a barycentric parameterization with a safety validation harness that falls back to a lattice seed on any failure. Directed gradient moves converge much faster than random perturbation, so we can afford many restarts within the time budget.
